summary: advanceOnCallback mirrors the established fire()/cancelActiveFor() structure (outer try/catch(Throwable) swallow, early-return no-op ladder, greppable LOG_* constants, ids/codes-only logging). Cross-file signatures verified against real code: resumeOnCallback(executionId, subscriberId, targetStepId):boolean, answerCallbackQuery(botId, callbackQueryId, text), findByChat, findByProjectIdAndStatus, logEvent, Button.type()/targetStepId(). No circular dependency (engine/sender do not depend back on the trigger service). answerCallbackQuery guaranteed on every exit path via finally. No heavy-resource duplication (all injected singletons).

findings.finding: stepById(snapshot, id) is duplicated from FunnelExecutionEngine's private static helper. The engine keeps it private, so it cannot be reused without widening its visibility; both classes navigate the snapshot independently.
findings.action: Accepted as-is. A 6-line trivial linear lookup; widening engine API surface to share it would couple the two classes more than the duplication costs. Documented in a code comment.

findings.finding: recordButtonClick runs AFTER the engine CAS already committed the advance; if eventService.logEvent throws, the outer catch(Throwable) logs LOG_CALLBACK_ERROR and lastButtonClicked may not be set, but the advance stays durable.
findings.action: Accepted by design. The event + lastButtonClicked are explicitly best-effort secondary writes (Decision 9 analytics hook); isolating their failure from the committed advance is the intended behaviour and is documented.
